newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Zimbabwe's Mugabe starts Cyprus visit.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe's Mugabe starts Cyprus visit.

text.p: Zimbabwe's President Robert Mugabe started a three-day official visit to Cyprus on Monday at the invitation of President Glafcos Clerides.

Mugabe, on his second visit to the eastern Mediterranean island that is a partner in the Commonwealth, will have official talks with Cypriot officials and address a special session of parliament on Tuesday.
"I'm here representing our people who recognise the people of Cyprus as being great friends and great allies," Mugabe told Clerides during an official welcoming ceremony at Larnaca airport.
The two countries enjoy close ties and Cyprus views Mugabe as a staunch supporter in the Commonwealth and Non-Aligned Movement of its positions regarding the division of the island.
Cyprus, which gained independence from Britain in 1960, has been divided since a Turkish invasion in 1974 sparked by a short-lived coup engineered by the military ruling in Greece at the time.

United Nations-led efforts to reunite the island as a bicommunal bizonal federation of Greek and Turkish Cypriots have so far failed to produce any results. Renewed efforts to bring the two sides to the negotiating table are expected to take place early this year.
"No people can enjoy total or full personality as a nation if others have tampered with that freexdom either directly or indirectly," said Mugabe, referring to the long-standing dispute.
"That freedom should not be interfered with through any guises or excuses that leave others in occupation of your territory," he told officials.

Cypriots on balconies clapped as the official motorcade passed on the road from the coastal town of Larnaca to capital Nicosia. Motorists with young children holding flowers stopped on the motorway, some holding pieces of cardboard welcoming Mugabe to Cyprus.
